## 固定收益開盤主論述

聯準會維持利率不變後，美國公債殖利率曲線在7月29日明顯分化。主席Kevin Warsh認為，市場殖利率上升已構成正在約束經濟的力量之一。2年期殖利率下降1.4個基點至4.274%，5年期則上升3.8個基點至4.409%，10年期攀升7.2個基點至4.679%，30年期更大漲11.3個基點至5.203%。短端以外呈現鮮明的熊市陡峭化：2年與10年期利差擴大8.6個基點至40.5個基點，2年與30年期利差則擴大12.7個基點至92.9個基點。

殖利率曲線的變化，反映市場將聯準會下次升息的時點，與長期通膨風險分開定價。聯邦公開市場委員會以9票對3票決定，連續第5次會議將目標利率區間維持在3.5%至3.75%。達拉斯聯準銀行總裁Lorie Logan、克里夫蘭聯準銀行總裁Beth Hammack及明尼亞波利斯聯準銀行總裁Neel Kashkari主張升息25個基點。在這場多年來最難預測的決策之一公布前，市場並未料到支持升息的陣營會如此龐大。

Warsh重申，聯準會仍致力於讓通膨回到2%，但未暗示9月可能升息。他反而主張，美國公債殖利率上升及金融情勢收緊，已代替央行完成部分緊縮工作。因此，依不同市場指標衡量，交易員將9月行動機率從週二收盤時接近確定，下修至約50%至60%；市場直到12月才完全反映一次升息。

短端的喘息並未延伸至其他天期。10年期損益兩平通膨率上升7.5個基點至2.27%，10年期實質殖利率則下降0.3個基點至2.409%；因此，10年期名目殖利率的升幅幾乎全由通膨補償增加所致，而非實質殖利率上升。30年期殖利率一度逼近5.23%，創2007年以來最高；投資人認為，口頭上的抗通膨決心、3張鷹派反對票及維持不變的政策利率，仍未化解長期物價風險。

美國與伊朗再度對峙，使這項區別更加重要。美方表示攔截伊朗對軍事基地的攻擊，總統Donald Trump並承諾強力回應；美國與沙烏地阿拉伯部隊也打擊了伊拉克境內受伊朗支持的武裝分子。布蘭特原油因而上漲7.37%至每桶$90.29，WTI上漲6.35%至$84.29。情勢升高驟然逆轉先前3個交易日支撐美國公債的油價回落，也重新帶來能源成本可能進一步推高既已偏高通膨的風險。

風險資產的表現也未顯示金融情勢趨於寬鬆。標普500指數下跌1.52%，那斯達克100指數下跌2.06%，費城半導體指數重挫5.33%，近1個月跌幅擴大至20.87%；VIX上漲13.45%至20.66。然而，長天期美國公債並未隨股市走弱而上漲，反而遭到拋售，顯示通膨及長天期風險補償壓過傳統避險需求。美元指數下跌0.59%，黃金期貨則上漲2.78%。

信用市場另為長端增添壓力。7月發行量創下歷年同期紀錄之際，紐約聯準銀行衡量投資級公司債市場失序程度的指標升至2023年11月以來最高。AI借款人是壓力核心：科技業信用保障成本普遍上升，CoreWeave改善一筆$26億貸款的條件，Proofpoint的放款人爭取到更嚴格的文件保障，而高盛則測試市場對另一筆可能達$54億的資料中心融資是否有興趣。在聯準會下一步尚未明朗前，美國公債波動與充沛的長天期公司債供給，已促使市場要求更高補償。

## 聯準會紓解短端壓力，卻失守長端

這次決策消除了7月意外升息的風險，卻幾乎沒有釐清9月的政策反應方式。決策公布前，交換市場反映立即升息25個基點的機率約為35%至40%；在受訪的100多名經濟學家中，除2人外均預期利率不變，因此這項機率異常偏高。決策移除這項尾端風險，讓2年期殖利率下降，但3張反對票也顯示，委員會內支持緊縮的陣營已經擴大。

反對者的身分尤其重要。Logan與Hammack先前已主張，持續的通膨可能需要利率略微上調；Kashkari加入，則顯示緊縮陣營不只包括市場最預期會反對的兩位地區聯準銀行總裁。不過，所有聯準會理事都與Warsh一同支持維持利率，形成理事會成員與3位具投票權地區聯準銀行總裁之間清楚可見的分歧。

會後聲明也無助於判斷委員會的中間立場。除利率決策外，聲明內容與6月大致相同，仍形容經濟活動穩健擴張、資本投資與生產力成長強勁，且通膨高於2%目標。Warsh堅稱聯準會並沒有較寬鬆的隱含通膨目標，並表示若整段預測期間的通膨持續偏高，利率可以成為解決方案的一部分，但他並未表示這項條件本身便足以觸發升息。

Warsh解釋維持利率的理由，對殖利率曲線更為關鍵。他表示，自上次會議以來，名目美國公債殖利率已經上升；市場之所以作出這些調整，部分是因為聯準會不再試圖影響殖利率。實際上，市場借款成本上升，使決策者無須立即調高隔夜利率，也能有時間觀察經濟。

這套說法卻讓長天期投資人面臨循環難題。若聯準會將市場推升的殖利率視為政策行動的替代品，市場就得在缺少過往可錨定近期預期的指引下，自行判斷所需的緊縮幅度。長端殖利率若回落，部分約束隨之消失；若維持高檔，即使期限溢價升高源於通膨偏高，聯準會也更沒有理由行動。結果是長端自行施加約束。

結果是，2年與30年期殖利率出現至少自1990年代中期以來幅度最大的幾次聯準會會後陡峭化之一。2年期殖利率小幅下降，30年期則上升11.3個基點。ICE美國政府1至3年期債券指數上漲0.06%，7至10年期指數下跌0.42%，20年以上指數下跌1.64%。長天期投資級公司債指數約跌1.2%至1.3%，反映其同時承受較高的美國公債利率敏感度及更不利的信用環境。

通膨拆解進一步印證市場的疑慮。10年期實質殖利率當日幾乎不變，損益兩平通膨率卻升至2.27%。此前1個月，名目10年期殖利率上升30.8個基點，實質殖利率也上升25個基點，顯示高昂的實質融資成本仍是這波廣泛拋售的重要部分；但就週三當日而言，新增的通膨補償才是主要邊際變化。

決策公布及殖利率曲線反轉也推升交易活動。FINRA記錄的美國公債面額交易量為$1.462兆，較週二增加11.4%，共計460,338筆。名目附息債交易量增加10.3%至$1.148兆；逾7年但不超過10年的附息債交易量增加30.4%至$1,911億，2年以下券種的周轉量則增加20.3%至$2,758億。這些數字反映最容易受會議影響的券種出現異常活躍的雙向調整，但無法辨識客戶的交易方向。

市場人士對這次維持利率究竟只是延後緊縮，還是削弱升息理由，看法不一。Brandywine Global的Jack McIntyre表示，除非通膨與就業明顯轉弱，3張反對票仍讓9月升息保有可能。Pimco的Tiffany Wilding認為，Warsh對物價穩定、經濟成長韌性及通膨高於目標的重視，與最終進一步收緊政策一致，只是時點未必如市場原先預期般早。Renaissance Macro的Neil Dutta則主張，主席只換來短暫喘息，接下來不是數據轉弱，就是必須在9月升息。

聯準會減少提供指引，使這些歧見更加突出。Apollo首席經濟學家Torsten Slok形容美國公債因此成為「溜溜球」市場，並指出記者會期間，9月升息機率從約70%降向50%。摩根大通資產管理的Bob Michele則聚焦反對票，認為即使委員會沒有行動，3票支持緊縮仍顯示官員正朝較高利率靠攏。

除下次政策時點外，美國公債供給也是長端另一項獨立問題。摩根大通策略師估計，未來4個會計年度將出現$3.7兆的融資缺口，並主張財政部最終必須弱化標售規模會在「至少未來幾季」保持穩定的保證。不過，他們仍預期官員會在即將到來的季度再融資中保留這項措辭，部分原因是避免在11月期中選舉前釋出長天期供給將增加的訊號。

這是具名機構的預測，並非已公布的融資決策。其重要性在於時點：短期指引維持穩定，可避免立即引發供給衝擊，卻也會延後正視未來融資需求。摩根大通警告，若刪除「至少」一詞，可能因期限溢價上升而使曲線變陡，類似2023年8月的市場反應。在30年期殖利率已高於5.2%的情況下，承認長天期供給還將增加的代價已經提高。

## 戰事重啟，能源通膨溢價回歸

聯準會會議前後，宏觀環境最明顯的變化是油價反轉。此前原油回落、美國與伊朗暫停攻擊，帶動美國公債連續3個交易日上漲。美方表示攔截伊朗突襲軍事基地，並與沙烏地阿拉伯部隊打擊伊拉克境內受德黑蘭支持的團體後，這段喘息隨即結束；Trump表示，美國將強力回擊伊朗。

布蘭特原油上漲7.37%至$90.29，WTI上漲6.35%至$84.29。油價雖未回到7月稍早高點，卻顯示外交休兵可能多快逆轉。布蘭特1個月累計仍上漲25.42%，WTI上漲21.75%。即使當日走勢代表衝突再度升高而非創下新高，這些累計漲幅仍使能源成為通膨的重要因素。

相較衝突初期，實體市場吸收另一場供應中斷的空間也更有限。荷莫茲海峽的流量數月來持續受阻，已使全球庫存下降；烏克蘭攻擊俄羅斯出口與加工基礎設施，加上紅海周邊與沙烏地阿拉伯相關航運所受威脅，又增加數個脆弱環節。部分煉油商為避開曼德海峽，已預訂繞行非洲南部的較長航線，既提高運輸成本，也讓油輪被占用更久。

風險與供給之間仍非線性關係。高額運費利潤可能吸引船舶重返危險航線，恢復部分運量並抑制漲價；但一旦攻擊得逞或安全情勢急遽惡化，船東也可能同樣迅速撤離。這解釋了原油為何在7月於約$70至超過$100之間擺盪，卻未能為決策者建立穩定的價格訊號。

週三各類資產的表現顯示，投資人主要把新一波油價衝擊視為通膨問題。10年期損益兩平通膨率上升，而實質殖利率大致不變，符合市場提高未來物價壓力補償的解讀。美元下跌0.59%，也未提供美元升值有時能對商品通膨形成的反向緊縮效果。

隨美元走弱及地緣政治風險回歸，黃金期貨上漲2.78%至$4,148.60。即使長天期美國公債殖利率上升，黃金仍能同步上漲，是因聯準會維持利率帶來的短端寬慰，以及市場對抗通膨資產需求回升，壓過長端利率上揚通常造成的壓力。戰爭爆發以來，黃金一度下跌逾五分之一，但之後仍守在$4,000附近；此前能源成本偏高已強化利率將在更長時間維持高檔的前景。

股市同時承受能源衝擊及科技業特有的賣壓。那斯達克100指數較6月高點下跌逾11%，進入修正區；半導體指數則連續第5天下跌，當日跌幅達5.33%。SK海力士獲利雖大幅成長，仍未達市場的高預期；其創紀錄的$310億資本支出計畫，更加深市場對AI產能成長可能快於其經濟回報的疑慮。南韓基準股指兩個交易日已下跌16%，促使當局承諾採取穩定市場措施，並收緊槓桿型交易所交易產品限制。

因此，美國收盤並非傳統的避險行情。標普500指數下跌1.52%、波動率上升，長天期美國公債卻也下跌。投資人一面降低對高估值科技股的曝險，一面要求政府債券提供更高通膨補償。兩者並行對經濟的約束大於任一走勢單獨發生：股票財富縮水，而用於訂價房貸、公司債及基礎設施融資的長期利率上升。

美元反應證實，儘管通膨前景惡化，聯準會維持利率仍移除了近期政策溢價。美元指數下跌0.59%，幅度大於彭博廣泛美元指標在決策後的0.3%跌幅。隨防範意外升息的避險部位解除，新興市場貨幣溫和上漲，但支撐能否持續仍取決於油價及全球風險情緒。美元走弱可減輕部分借款人的外部融資壓力，卻無法抵銷美國長端殖利率上升對美元債務的影響。

## AI借款壓力已超越個別交易

AI支出熱潮對信用市場的影響，已更清楚地反映在官方壓力指標、衍生性商品、貸款及潛在債券供給上。紐約聯準銀行的公司債市場困境指數顯示，整體市場相對穩定，但投資級債券轉差。廣泛指數由6月底的0.16降至7月的0.15，高評級分項卻由0.25升至0.30，並於7月17日觸及0.33，創2023年11月以來最高。

這項分歧之所以重要，是因為壓力正出現在被視為高品質、且發行量最大的債券領域。7月投資級債券發行額約$1,320億，創歷年同期紀錄，大型科技公司及資料中心融資占了很大比重。投資級債券利差由7月初的74個基點擴大至約80個基點，雖仍處於歷史低檔，但投資人反覆承接巨額發行後，市場運作環境已變得較不利。

信用違約交換顯示，科技業借款人的信用表現日益分化。Oracle的5年期信用保障成本超過215個基點，高於2025年底約145個基點，其2054年到期債券殖利率則升至7.8%，今年來上升近1個百分點。SpaceX信用保障成本約為185個基點，較合約6月開始交易時高逾50%。Meta的CDS由年底約56個基點升近95個基點，Amazon由36升至約68個基點；Alphabet自3月開始活躍交易時約50個基點，升至65個基點以上。Microsoft自2017年以來未曾發債，且仍保有AAA評級，升幅較小，由35個基點升至約53個基點。

CoreWeave仍是大型AI相關信用中最弱的一家。其5年期信用保障成本超過855個基點，公司同時尋求一筆$26億的延後動用貸款，為Anthropic、Jane Street及Hudson River Trading等客戶所需的運算能力提供資金。這筆融資可分期動用，僅就實際借款金額計息，並以客戶的照付不議合約作為支持。

即便如此，投資人仍要求大幅讓利。定價討論中的利差較原先最多擴大125個基點，最高達基準利率加550個基點，發行價格則由面額的99%降至97%。CoreWeave也在週四認購截止前加強債權人保障。此前1個月，其信用保障成本已上升逾五成，市場對預期每年超過$340億的基礎設施支出能否持續也愈發擔憂。

壓力也延伸至可能發行的投資級基礎設施債務。高盛正在探詢市場對一筆潛在$54億融資的需求，標的是喬治亞州一座由黑石支持、出租給Microsoft的QTS資料中心。研議中的融資組合包括約$49億的5年期擔保債券及$5億的7年期貸款，但時點與條款仍在討論。

QTS現有債務的表現，說明新交易為何可能必須讓利。7月稍早發行的一筆$32.5億貸款，定價為每1元面額99.5分，之後已跌至97.75分。QTS於4月首次發行的$46億高評級債券，發行時利差接近高於美國公債138個基點，如今已擴大至約239個基點。這些次級市場價位提高新交易成功售出所需的殖利率，也使其能否完成取決於科技信用交易能否趨於平穩。

借款人也把更多控制權交給放款人。投資人要求加強防範債務管理操作的保障後，Thoma Bravo旗下Proofpoint修改一筆$50億的修約展期交易。這家資安公司新增「全方位阻擋條款」，意在防止抵押品被移出既有債權人的求償範圍；同時禁止私下協商回購債務，並修改約24項條款。這筆交易將把2028年到期日延至2030年。

歐洲槓桿融資市場也出現要求提早償還本金的類似趨勢。Paysafe提出每年償還原貸款金額的5%，以換取將$8.14億及€5.86億債務的到期日延長2年至2030年。這些貸款以高於基準利率500個基點行銷；投資人按面額95%提供資金，未來則可能收回全額本金。放款人評估Cinven旗下think-cell未來的展期時，也要求在其€7.2億貸款中加入攤還安排。

全球金融危機後，這類強制還本條款在歐洲並不常見。如今再度出現，反映市場擔心目前獲利豐厚的軟體公司，可能在貸款到期前失去定價能力或市占率。CLO經理人面臨相互衝突的誘因：新供給短缺有利借款人取得融資，但AI帶來的衝擊，以及大量軟體業貸款集中於2028年到期，也使債權人有理由趁目前要求現金還本及更嚴格的文件保障。

只要殖利率與結構足以吸引買方，初級市場仍然開放。SoftBank完成¥900億機構債定價，包括¥800億3年期債券，利差為高於日本公債165個基點，以及¥100億5年期債券，利差為190個基點。兩券票息分別為3.270%及3.886%，是日本企業發行人在今年相同期限支付的最高票息。升息環境下，投資人偏好較短天期，因此3年期規模由原訂¥500億提高；5年期認購需求約為發行額的1.2倍。

印度國家銀行也在近2年後重返其他第一類資本市場，募得₹469.1億。這批永續證券票息為7.75%，5年後可贖回，投標金額超過₹300億基礎發行規模的2倍。截至3月止的1年內，SBI貸款餘額成長近17%至超過₹49兆，此次發行可補充其資本。

這些完成的交易並未否定AI信用惡化。SBI是為廣泛貸款成長籌措監管資本；SoftBank則支付處於國內歷史高檔的票息，並把發行集中於買方偏好的較短期限。相較之下，美國科技融資市場反覆推出資料中心交易，正爭奪承接長天期資產的資金，同時投資人也開始質疑自由現金流、客戶集中度及相關資產的報酬。

另一項私募信貸議題，也使風險如何進入受監管機構的資產負債表受到檢視。監管申報揭露與Guggenheim有關的資產後，評級機構重新計算Delaware Life的關係企業資產，估計占總資產約40%至42%，遠高於先前申報的約3%至5%。標普與惠譽均將其展望調降至負向。外界擔心的不只是資產表現，也包括與共同控制實體相關的投資是否採取一致分類，以及是否有足夠資本支持。更廣泛的監管審查，可能減緩關係資產管理公司把私人貸款配置給保險公司的管道。

## 全球通膨數據使緊縮週期更加複雜

美國以外，澳洲核心通膨低於預期，帶動最明顯的債券漲勢。第2季截尾平均消費者物價年增3.6%，低於3.7%的預估；季增率為0.8%，也低於預期的0.9%。對政策敏感的3年期政府公債殖利率下降11個基點，澳幣一度下跌0.5%，交易員並將2026年再度升息的機率由逾90%降至約50%。

澳洲央行今年前3次會議均升息，這份數據讓其在8月11日按兵不動的空間增加，但尚不足以證明國內通膨已回到目標。可貿易品價格較上年同期上升1.5%，受油價下跌及暫時性燃油稅減免幫助；不可貿易品通膨則仍達4.9%。央行總裁Michele Bullock先前已警告，通膨偏離2%至3%目標區間愈久，理事會的憂慮便愈深。

日本在7月31日日本央行會議前釋出不同的薪資訊號。厚生勞動省諮詢小組建議，本會計年度全國平均最低時薪提高4.9%至¥1,176。增加¥55將是歷來第二大增幅，雖低於前一年的6.3%。各地主管機關仍須自行訂定標準，新下限才會自10月起陸續生效。

這項建議將涵蓋逾5,000萬名勞工。日本最大工會聯合會所代表的員工，平均年度薪資已連續第3年增加逾5%。對日本央行而言，薪資成長的廣度相當重要，因為大型企業以外的薪酬提高，將支撐消費並形成更持久的薪資—物價循環。日本央行6月才將利率升至1%，市場仍普遍預期本次維持不變；但若日圓疲弱造成的輸入性通膨持續，薪資證據將支持進一步正常化。

國內債市已讓耐心推動正常化付出代價。日本政府年金投資基金截至3月止1年內的日本債券投資虧損5.1%，即使整體資產報酬率達16.5%，仍在5年來首次聘任主動式國內債券經理人。基金委任Asset Management One、三菱日聯信託銀行及三井住友信託資產管理，尋求高於基準的報酬，並更積極管理期限及信用曝險。10年期日本公債殖利率7月初曾升至2.9%，其1年高低區間已由2017年約14個基點擴大至約100個基點。

歐元區的薪資訊號較為溫和。歐洲央行追蹤指標預測，協商薪資在2026年下半年成長2.6%，2027年第1季成長2.7%，遠低於2024年的5.2%高峰。2027年初增速部分回升，源於一次性給付消退所造成的機械性效果，而非新一波薪資衝擊。歐洲央行總裁Christine Lagarde表示，近期指標仍符合薪資逐步放緩的趨勢，尚未顯示能源價格引發第二輪效應。

這降低、但沒有消除歐洲央行再度升息的壓力。官員6月升息後維持利率不變，若通膨前景未改善，仍準備再度緊縮。包括斯洛伐克央行總裁Peter Kazimir在內的部分決策者警告，若等到薪資轉嫁已清楚浮現才行動，政策可能為時已晚。新的追蹤資料更支持目前能源衝擊尚未造成類似2022年薪資—物價循環的判斷。

英國央行7月30日決策前，家庭與企業借款仍具韌性。6月房貸核准件數由5月逾2年低點回升至58,200件，高於57,100件的預測，但仍低於61,435件的6個月平均。無擔保信貸淨額由£17億增至£18億，其中信用卡借款增加£3億至£9億；企業放款則由£11億增至£15億。

這些資金流量與顯著提高的融資成本並存。7月29日平均5年期固定房貸利率達5.66%，高於美國與以色列2月攻擊伊朗前的4.83%。英國央行預計會在總體成長疲弱與能源通膨再起之間權衡，並維持利率不變；但借款數據幾乎沒有證據顯示，高利率已造成家庭或企業信用急遽收縮。

加拿大央行的討論呈現更為勢均力敵的分歧。官員7月稍早連續第6次會議將政策利率維持在2.25%，並認為隨經濟適應近期衝擊，成長疲弱與通膨之間的取捨已經減輕。央行預期經濟成長將由2026年的0.7%，加速至2027年與2028年的1.8%，但理事會成員對復甦能否擴大及延續意見不一。

部分加拿大央行官員也注意到中期通膨預期逐步上升。閒置產能、單位勞動成本成長緩慢及租金通膨走弱，正在抑制服務價格，抵銷部分汽油價格上漲的影響。該次會議早於美國與伊朗再度升高衝突，也早於Trump威脅對加拿大商品加徵關稅；這使央行原先認為可以從容按兵不動的判斷，同時面臨成長與通膨兩端的新衝擊。

巴西則在市場預期8月5日降息前公布較強勁的勞動數據。6月新增145,161個正式就業職位，高於115,000個的預估中位數，主要由服務業及農業帶動。儘管如此，7月上半月通膨仍由6月中旬的4.8%降至4.52%，當月價格僅上升0.06%。經濟學家依然預期央行將連續第4次降息25個基點至14%，但就業強勁及選舉前的財政支持，不利於展開長期寬鬆週期。

## 後續市場意義

下一批美國通膨與勞動成本數據，將決定7月維持利率究竟只是暫停，還是聯準會將更持久地依賴市場自行收緊。7月31日公布的第2季就業成本指數，是檢驗國內薪資壓力最明確的既定事件。若數據強勁，即使能源衝擊仍然波動，也將支持3位反對者主張收緊政策；若數據偏弱，則有利於支持先觀察市場殖利率上升如何影響經濟活動的理事。

美國公債曲線兩端目前各有不同考驗。2年期殖利率反映9月升息的急迫性下降，10年及30年期殖利率上升則反映市場要求更高的通膨與長天期風險補償。若後續數據強化立即升息的理由，短端可能逆轉，而長期通膨補償不一定需要再升高。若數據轉弱但油價維持高檔，曲線仍可能保持陡峭，因為聯準會延後回應並不能消除長期物價風險。

在數據作出判斷前，美國與伊朗的衝突仍可能改變這項分布。若外交關係恢復，荷莫茲海峽通行也更為可靠，損益兩平通膨率所受壓力將會減輕。若軍事設施、油輪或替代出口航線再遭攻擊，聯準會面對的將是1個月內已上漲逾20%的原油，以及長端不再因股市下跌而自動上漲的美國公債市場。

季度再融資將使供給問題進入同一場討論。若標售規模指引維持不變，可避免立即證實市場對長天期發行增加的預期。任何讓較大規模附息債標售更快到來的調整，都將考驗30年期殖利率高於5.2%是否足以補償投資人，尤其財政借款與公司債發行正在爭奪相同的長天期資金。

AI信用市場面臨更迫近的交易期限。CoreWeave把$26億貸款利差提高至高於基準利率最多550個基點、發行折價降至97分並加強文件保障後，認購將於週四截止。在這些條件下的需求，將顯示投資人是否認為照付不議合約足以防範槓桿擴張週期，抑或仍要求更多補償。

可能達$54億的QTS融資，是下一項高評級資料中心債務考驗。市場將以QTS近期貸款價格下跌，以及其4月債券相對美國公債利差由約138個基點擴大至239個基點為基準，評估交易能否完成。延後發行可讓發行人保留彈性；若交易完成，則會確立7月高評級債券供給創紀錄後所需的新券發行溢酬。

英國央行將於7月30日作出決策。市場普遍預期維持利率不變，因此通膨評估及如何看待能源成本上升，比政策利率本身更為重要。房貸利率已達5.66%，但房貸核准件數仍然回升，消費者與企業借款也持續增加；官員因此只有有限證據可證明現有約束已使需求明顯轉弱。

日本央行接著於7月31日決策。6月將利率升至1%後，本次仍預期維持不變，但最低工資建議調升4.9%，更有力地證明薪資成長正向外擴散。政策指引必須在這股薪資動能、高昂進口成本的影響，以及已促使大型國內退休基金轉向主動管理日本公債的市場波動之間取得平衡。

澳洲央行下一次會議訂於8月11日，屆時將檢驗較溫和的截尾平均CPI是否足以終結今年的緊縮週期。通膨低於預期及3年期殖利率下降11個基點，均有利於央行耐心等待；但非貿易財通膨仍達4.9%，油價壓力也再度上升，因此再次升息只是機率降低，並未被排除。

對信用投資人而言，更廣泛的考驗在於重新定價是否仍集中於AI相關借款人，抑或會進一步損害投資級市場運作。紐約聯準銀行的高評級債券困境指標上升、科技業CDS利差擴大、貸款定價對投資人更優厚，以及放款人保障增強，都顯示借款人的議價能力下降。SBI與SoftBank仍能取得資金，證明資本並未消失，但市場正更嚴格區分每筆交易的價格、期限及文件條款。

7月29日收盤後，市場對已作出的決策少了一些不確定性，對緊縮將如何落實卻增添更多疑問。聯準會沒有提高隔夜利率，短端上漲、美元下跌；油價、損益兩平通膨率及長端則朝相反方向變動。在通膨數據、能源供給或政策指引提供更穩固的錨之前，市場本身正在為長期借款訂出更高價格。

overall_summary.headline: 聯準會按兵不動帶動短端上漲，通膨風險則引發長端拋售
overall_summary.session_narrative:
聯準會連續第5次會議維持利率不變後，美國公債走勢明顯分化。主席Kevin Warsh未暗示9月升息，並表示市場殖利率上升已在約束經濟，帶動2年期殖利率下降1.4個基點至4.274%。10年期殖利率則上升7.2個基點至4.679%，30年期大漲11.3個基點至5.203%，使2年與30年期利差擴大12.7個基點。

長端拋售主要由通膨補償帶動：10年期損益兩平通膨率上升7.5個基點至2.27%，實質殖利率則近乎不變。3位聯準會官員主張升息25個基點；美國與伊朗再度交戰，也使布蘭特原油上漲7.37%、WTI上漲6.35%，逆轉此前3個交易日支撐美國公債的油價回落。

股市走弱並未帶來傳統避險漲勢。科技股領跌、波動率上升，長天期美國公債卻也下跌，反映投資人要求更高的通膨及長天期風險補償。7月投資級債券發行量創紀錄，加上AI融資成本日益提高，也為長天期信用資產增添壓力。
overall_summary.summary: 聯準會將利率維持在3.5%至3.75%，降低9月升息的急迫性；但3張鷹派反對票、依賴市場自行收緊，以及美國與伊朗再度交戰，仍大幅推升通膨補償與長天期美國公債殖利率。

## Opening Fixed-Income Thesis

Treasuries split sharply across the curve on July 29 after the Federal Reserve left rates unchanged and Chair Kevin Warsh treated higher market yields as part of the restraint already working on the economy. The 2-year yield declined 1.4 basis points to 4.274%, but the 5-year rose 3.8 basis points to 4.409%, the 10-year climbed 7.2 basis points to 4.679% and the 30-year jumped 11.3 basis points to 5.203%. The result was a pronounced bear steepening beyond the front end: the 2s10s spread widened 8.6 basis points to 40.5 basis points, while 2s30s increased 12.7 basis points to 92.9 basis points.

The curve move separated the timing of the next Fed increase from the market’s longer-term inflation judgment. The Federal Open Market Committee voted 9-3 to retain a 3.5% to 3.75% target range for a fifth consecutive meeting. Dallas Fed President Lorie Logan, Cleveland Fed President Beth Hammack and Minneapolis Fed President Neel Kashkari preferred a quarter-point increase, a larger dissenting bloc than markets had expected before one of the least predictable decisions in years.

Warsh repeated that the Fed remains committed to returning inflation to 2%, but declined to signal that an increase could come in September. He instead argued that higher Treasury yields and tighter financial conditions had already performed some of the central bank’s work. Traders consequently reduced the probability of a September move toward roughly 50% to 60%, depending on the market measure, from expectations near certainty at Tuesday’s close. A hike was not fully priced until December.

That relief was confined to short maturities. The 10-year breakeven rate rose 7.5 basis points to 2.27%, while the 10-year real yield slipped 0.3 basis point to 2.409%. Almost all of the nominal 10-year selloff therefore came through higher inflation compensation rather than an increase in the inflation-adjusted yield. The 30-year yield briefly approached 5.23%, its highest since 2007, as investors judged that verbal resolve, three hawkish dissents and an unchanged policy rate had not resolved the longer-run price risk.

The renewed U.S.-Iran confrontation made that distinction more consequential. Brent rose 7.37% to $90.29 and WTI gained 6.35% to $84.29 after the U.S. said it intercepted an Iranian attack on military bases and President Donald Trump promised a forceful response. U.S. and Saudi forces also struck Iran-backed militants in Iraq. The escalation abruptly reversed the oil relief that had supported Treasuries during the previous three sessions and restored the possibility that energy costs will reinforce already-elevated inflation.

Risk assets offered no offsetting message of easy financial conditions. The S&P 500 fell 1.52%, the Nasdaq 100 lost 2.06% and the Philadelphia Semiconductor Index dropped 5.33%, extending its 1-month decline to 20.87%. The VIX rose 13.45% to 20.66. Yet long Treasuries sold off rather than rallying with weaker equities, underscoring that inflation and duration compensation dominated the usual haven response. The dollar index fell 0.59%, while gold futures gained 2.78%.

Credit markets added a separate source of pressure at longer maturities. The New York Fed’s measure of investment-grade corporate-bond dysfunction rose to its highest level since November 2023 as July issuance reached a record for the month. AI borrowers were central to the strain: protection costs rose across technology credits, CoreWeave sweetened a $2.6 billion loan, lenders extracted stronger documentation from Proofpoint, and Goldman Sachs tested interest in another possible $5.4 billion data-center financing. The combination of Treasury volatility and abundant long-duration corporate supply left the market demanding more compensation even before the Fed’s next move became clear.

## The Fed Relieves the Front End and Loses the Long End

The immediate policy outcome resolved the risk of a surprise July increase but did little to define the reaction function for September. Before the announcement, swaps had assigned roughly a 35% to 40% probability to an immediate quarter-point move, unusually high for a meeting at which all but two of more than 100 surveyed economists expected no change. The decision removed that tail risk, allowing the 2-year yield to fall, but the three dissents established that support for tightening had broadened inside the committee.

The identities of the dissenters mattered. Logan and Hammack had already argued that persistent inflation could require modestly higher rates. Kashkari’s addition showed that the tightening camp extended beyond the two regional presidents most widely expected to object. All Fed governors nevertheless joined Warsh in voting to hold, leaving a visible split between the board and three voting reserve-bank presidents.

The post-meeting statement offered little help in locating the committee’s center. It was otherwise unchanged from June, retaining the characterization of economic activity as expanding at a solid pace, capital investment and productivity growth as strong, and inflation as elevated relative to the 2% objective. Warsh insisted that there was no softer implicit inflation goal and said rates could be part of the solution if inflation remained elevated through the forecast period. He stopped short of making that condition sufficient by itself.

His explanation for holding proved more important for the curve. Warsh said nominal Treasury rates had risen since the prior meeting and that markets had made those decisions partly because the Fed had stepped back from trying to influence them. In effect, higher market borrowing costs gave policymakers time to observe the economy without raising the overnight rate immediately.

That argument created a circular problem for long-duration investors. If the Fed regards a market-led rise in yields as a substitute for policy action, the market must decide how much tightening is needed without the guidance that previously anchored near-term expectations. If longer yields fall, some of that restraint disappears. If they remain high, the Fed has less reason to act even though elevated inflation is the source of the term premium. The long end responded by imposing the restraint itself.

The result was one of the largest post-Fed steepenings between 2- and 30-year yields since at least the mid-1990s. The 2-year yield’s modest decline contrasted with an 11.3-basis-point rise in the 30-year. The ICE U.S. Government 1–3 Year Bond Index gained 0.06%, while the 7–10 Year Index lost 0.42% and the 20-plus-year index fell 1.64%. Long investment-grade corporate indices declined by roughly 1.2% to 1.3%, reflecting their combined exposure to higher Treasury duration and a more difficult credit backdrop.

The inflation decomposition reinforced the market’s skepticism. The 10-year real yield was essentially unchanged on the day, but the breakeven rate rose to 2.27%. Over the preceding month, the nominal 10-year yield had increased 30.8 basis points and the real yield 25 basis points, showing that high real financing costs remained an important part of the broader selloff. On Wednesday itself, however, renewed inflation compensation was the dominant marginal change.

Trading activity rose with the decision and the curve reversal. FINRA recorded $1.462 trillion of Treasury par activity, 11.4% more than Tuesday, across 460,338 trades. Nominal-coupon activity increased 10.3% to $1.148 trillion. Activity in coupons longer than 7 years through 10 years rose 30.4% to $191.1 billion, while turnover in maturities of 2 years or less increased 20.3% to $275.8 billion. The figures capture unusually heavy two-way adjustment in the sectors most exposed to the meeting but do not identify customer direction.

Market participants differed over whether the hold postponed or weakened the tightening case. Brandywine Global’s Jack McIntyre said the three dissents left September in play unless inflation and employment softened materially. Pimco’s Tiffany Wilding judged Warsh’s emphasis on price stability, resilient growth and above-target inflation consistent with eventual firming, though not necessarily as soon as markets had expected. Renaissance Macro’s Neil Dutta argued that the chairman had bought only a temporary reprieve and would need either softer data or a September increase.

The Fed’s retreat from guidance magnified those disagreements. Apollo Chief Economist Torsten Slok described the resulting Treasury swings as a “yo-yo” market, noting that the probability of a September increase moved from around 70% toward 50% during the press conference. Bob Michele of JPMorgan Asset Management focused instead on the dissenters, arguing that three votes to tighten showed officials migrating toward higher rates even though the committee did not act.

Treasury supply adds another long-end issue independent of the next policy date. JPMorgan strategists estimated that a $3.7 trillion funding gap will emerge over the next four fiscal years and argued that the Treasury eventually needs to soften its assurance that auction sizes will remain steady for “at least the next several quarters.” They nevertheless expect officials to leave that language unchanged at the coming quarterly refunding, partly to avoid signaling larger duration supply before the November midterm elections.

That is an attributed forecast, not an announced financing decision. Its significance lies in the timing problem: stable near-term guidance could avoid an immediate supply shock, but it would also defer recognition of future funding needs. JPMorgan warned that removing “at least” could steepen the curve by increasing the term premium, similar to the market reaction in August 2023. With the 30-year yield already above 5.2%, the cost of acknowledging additional long supply has increased.

## Renewed Fighting Restores the Energy Inflation Premium

The oil reversal was the clearest change in the macro setting around the Fed meeting. Treasuries had rallied for three sessions as crude retreated and the U.S. and Iran paused attacks. That respite ended after the U.S. said it intercepted a surprise Iranian assault on military bases and conducted strikes with Saudi forces against Tehran-backed groups in Iraq. Trump said the U.S. would hit Iran hard in response.

Brent’s 7.37% jump to $90.29 and WTI’s 6.35% rise to $84.29 did not return crude to the highs reached earlier in July, but the move showed how quickly a diplomatic pause could reverse. Brent remained 25.42% higher over a month and WTI 21.75% higher. Those cumulative gains kept energy relevant to inflation even though the daily change represented renewed escalation rather than a fresh peak.

The physical market also had less room to absorb another disruption than at the beginning of the conflict. Months of interrupted flows through the Strait of Hormuz had reduced global inventories. Ukrainian attacks on Russian export and processing infrastructure and threats to Saudi-linked shipping around the Red Sea created additional points of vulnerability. Some refiners had already booked longer routes around southern Africa to avoid Bab el-Mandeb, increasing transport costs and tying up tankers for longer periods.

The relationship between risk and supply remained nonlinear. High freight profits can draw vessels back into dangerous routes, restoring some flows and tempering price gains. A successful attack or a sharp deterioration in security can cause owners to withdraw just as quickly. That explains why crude has moved between roughly $70 and above $100 during July without establishing a stable price signal for policymakers.

Wednesday’s market composition showed investors treating the renewed oil shock primarily as an inflation problem. The rise in the 10-year breakeven alongside an essentially unchanged real yield was consistent with greater compensation for future price pressure. The dollar’s 0.59% decline did not provide the countervailing tightening that a stronger U.S. currency sometimes delivers against commodity inflation.

Gold rose 2.78% to $4,148.60 in futures trading as the dollar weakened and geopolitical risk returned. The metal’s gain coexisted with higher long Treasury yields because the front-end relief from the Fed hold and the renewed demand for inflation protection outweighed the usual pressure from rising long rates. Gold had also held around the $4,000 area after falling more than a fifth since the war began, as elevated energy costs had previously strengthened the higher-for-longer rates outlook.

Equities absorbed both the energy shock and a technology-specific selloff. The Nasdaq 100 entered correction territory, falling more than 11% from its June high, while the semiconductor index lost 5.33% for a fifth consecutive decline. SK Hynix’s earnings fell short of elevated expectations even though profit increased sharply, and its record $31 billion capital-spending plan intensified concern that AI capacity could grow faster than its economic return. South Korea’s benchmark had fallen 16% over two sessions, prompting authorities to promise market-stabilization measures and tighter limits on leveraged exchange-traded products.

The U.S. close was therefore not a conventional flight to safety. The S&P 500 lost 1.52% and volatility rose, but long Treasuries also fell. Investors were reducing exposure to expensive technology shares while demanding more inflation compensation from government bonds. That combination is more restrictive for the economy than either move alone: equity wealth weakened, and the long rates used to price mortgages, corporate debt and infrastructure finance rose.

The dollar’s reaction confirmed that the Fed hold removed an immediate policy premium even as the inflation outlook deteriorated. The dollar index’s 0.59% fall was larger than the 0.3% decline in Bloomberg’s broader dollar gauge following the decision. Emerging-market currencies gained modestly as the surprise-hike hedge unwound, though the support was conditional on oil and global risk sentiment. A weaker dollar can ease external financing pressure for some borrowers, but it does not neutralize the effect of higher long U.S. yields on dollar debt.

## AI Borrowing Strain Moves Beyond Individual Deals

The credit-market consequences of the AI spending boom became more visible across official stress measures, derivatives, loans and prospective bond supply. The New York Fed’s Corporate Bond Market Distress Index showed relative stability for the overall market but a deterioration in investment grade. The broad index eased to 0.15 in July from 0.16 in late June, while its high-grade component rose to 0.30 from 0.25 and touched 0.33 on July 17, the highest since November 2023.

The divergence matters because it identifies strain inside the sector producing the largest volume of ostensibly high-quality borrowing. Roughly $132 billion of investment-grade bonds were issued in July, a record for the month, with Big Tech and data-center financing contributing heavily. Investment-grade spreads widened to about 80 basis points from 74 at the start of July. They remained low by historical standards, but the market’s functioning had become less favorable as investors absorbed repeated jumbo offerings.

Credit-default swaps showed growing differentiation among technology borrowers. Oracle’s 5-year protection cost exceeded 215 basis points, up from about 145 at the end of 2025, while the yield on its 2054 bonds reached 7.8%, almost a percentage point higher this year. SpaceX protection traded around 185 basis points, more than 50% above its level when the contracts began trading in June. Meta CDS rose toward 95 basis points from about 56 at year-end, Amazon’s to roughly 68 from 36 and Alphabet’s above 65 from about 50 when active trading began in March. Microsoft, which has not issued bonds since 2017 and retains AAA ratings, experienced a smaller increase to about 53 basis points from 35.

CoreWeave remained the weakest large AI-related credit. Its 5-year protection cost exceeded 855 basis points, while the company sought a $2.6 billion delayed-draw loan to fund computing capacity for customers including Anthropic, Jane Street and Hudson River Trading. The financing can be drawn over time, with interest charged only on borrowed amounts, and is supported by take-or-pay customer contracts.

Investors still required materially richer terms. Pricing discussions widened by as much as 125 basis points to as much as 550 basis points over the benchmark, and the issue discount moved to 97 cents from 99. CoreWeave also strengthened creditor protections before Thursday’s order deadline. The concessions followed a month in which its protection cost had risen by more than half and concern increased about the sustainability of more than $34 billion in expected annual infrastructure spending.

The pressure extended to prospective investment-grade infrastructure debt. Goldman Sachs was gauging demand for a possible $5.4 billion financing for a Blackstone-backed QTS data center in Georgia leased to Microsoft. The contemplated package included about $4.9 billion of 5-year secured bonds and a $500 million 7-year loan, although timing and terms remained under discussion.

Outstanding QTS debt showed why the new transaction could require a concession. A $3.25 billion loan issued earlier in July had fallen to 97.75 cents after pricing at 99.5. QTS’s $4.6 billion debut high-grade bond, sold in April at almost 138 basis points over Treasuries, had widened to about 239 basis points. Those secondary levels raise the yield needed for another deal to clear and make execution dependent on calmer technology-credit trading.

Borrowers were also yielding control to lenders. Thoma Bravo’s Proofpoint revised a $5 billion amend-and-extend transaction after investors demanded stronger protection against liability-management exercises. The cybersecurity company added an “omni blocker” intended to prevent collateral from being shifted beyond existing creditors’ reach, prohibited privately negotiated debt buybacks and altered roughly two dozen provisions. The transaction would extend a 2028 maturity to 2030.

European leveraged finance showed a parallel move toward earlier principal repayment. Paysafe offered to repay 5% of its original loan amounts annually to secure 2-year maturity extensions on $814 million and €586 million of debt to 2030. The loans were marketed at 500 basis points over the benchmark, with investors lending 95% of face value while potentially receiving repayment of the full amount. Lenders considering a future extension for Cinven-owned think-cell also wanted amortization added to its €720 million loan.

Such mandatory repayments have been uncommon in Europe since the global financial crisis. Their return reflects concern that highly profitable software companies today could lose pricing power or market share before loans mature. CLO managers face competing incentives: a shortage of new supply supports borrower access, but AI disruption and the large concentration of software loans coming due in 2028 give creditors reason to demand cash repayment and tighter documents while they can.

Primary markets remained open where yield and structure were sufficient. SoftBank priced ¥90 billion of institutional bonds, comprising ¥80 billion of 3-year notes at 165 basis points over Japanese government bonds and ¥10 billion of 5-year debt at a 190-basis-point spread. Coupons of 3.270% and 3.886% were the highest paid this year by a domestic corporate issuer at those maturities. The 3-year tranche was increased from an initially planned ¥50 billion as investors favored shorter debt in a rising-rate environment; demand for the 5-year tranche was about 1.2 times the amount issued.

State Bank of India also returned to its Additional Tier 1 market after almost 2 years, raising 46.91 billion rupees. The perpetual securities carry a 7.75% coupon and a 5-year call, and bids exceeded twice the 30 billion-rupee base size. The issuance supports capital after SBI’s loan book grew nearly 17% to more than 49 trillion rupees in the year through March.

Those completed transactions did not contradict the deterioration in AI credit. SBI raised regulatory capital against broad loan growth, while SoftBank paid historically high domestic coupons and concentrated issuance in the shorter maturity preferred by buyers. In U.S. technology finance, by contrast, repeated data-center transactions are competing for long-duration balance sheets at the same time that investors are questioning free cash flow, customer concentration and the return on the underlying assets.

A separate private-credit issue added scrutiny of how risk reaches regulated balance sheets. Rating agencies recalculated Delaware Life’s affiliated assets at roughly 40% to 42% of total assets, up from previously reported levels around 3% to 5%, after regulatory disclosures related to Guggenheim-linked holdings. S&P and Fitch revised their outlooks to negative. The concern is not merely asset performance but whether investments tied to entities under common control were classified consistently and backed by adequate capital. Broader regulatory review could slow the channel through which affiliated asset managers place private loans with insurers.

## Global Inflation Data Complicate the Tightening Cycle

Outside the U.S., Australia produced the clearest bond rally as core inflation came in below expectations. The annual trimmed-mean consumer-price measure rose 3.6% in Q2, compared with a 3.7% estimate, while the quarterly increase was 0.8% rather than the expected 0.9%. The policy-sensitive 3-year government-bond yield fell 11 basis points, the Australian dollar declined as much as 0.5% and traders reduced the probability of another 2026 increase to about 50% from more than 90%.

The release gave the Reserve Bank of Australia more room to hold on Aug. 11 after raising rates at its first three meetings of the year. It did not establish that domestic inflation had returned to target. Tradable prices rose 1.5% from a year earlier, helped by lower oil and temporary fuel-tax relief, while non-tradable inflation remained 4.9%. Governor Michele Bullock had already warned that the longer inflation remained outside the 2% to 3% band, the greater the board’s concern.

Japan supplied a different wage signal ahead of the Bank of Japan’s July 31 meeting. A Labor Ministry advisory panel recommended increasing the nationwide average minimum hourly wage by 4.9% to ¥1,176 for the current fiscal year. The ¥55 gain would be the second-largest on record, though slower than the previous year’s 6.3% increase. Regional authorities must set their own rates before the new floors begin taking effect gradually in October.

The recommendation would cover more than 50 million workers and follows average annual pay increases above 5% for a third year among employees represented by Japan’s largest labor federation. For the BOJ, the breadth of the wage gains matters because stronger pay outside major corporations would support consumption and a more durable wage-price cycle. The bank is still widely expected to hold after raising its rate to 1% in June, but the wage evidence supports the case for further normalization if imported inflation from the weak yen persists.

The domestic bond market has already imposed a cost on patient normalization. Japan’s Government Pension Investment Fund hired active domestic bond managers for the first time in 5 years after losing 5.1% on Japanese debt in the year through March, even as its overall assets returned 16.5%. The fund appointed Asset Management One, Mitsubishi UFJ Trust & Banking and Sumitomo Mitsui Trust Asset Management to seek returns above benchmarks and manage maturity and credit exposure more actively. Ten-year JGB yields had reached 2.9% in early July, and their 1-year high-low range had widened to around 100 basis points from about 14 basis points in 2017.

Euro-area wage evidence was more benign. The European Central Bank’s tracker projected negotiated pay growth of 2.6% in the second half of 2026 and 2.7% in Q1 2027, far below the 5.2% peak in 2024. Part of the acceleration into early 2027 reflects the mechanical fading of one-off payments rather than a renewed wage shock. ECB President Christine Lagarde said recent indicators remained consistent with a gradual wage slowdown and had not yet shown second-round effects from energy.

That reduces, but does not eliminate, the pressure for another ECB increase. Officials held rates after raising them in June and are prepared to tighten again if the inflation outlook fails to improve. Some policymakers, including Slovakia’s Peter Kazimir, have warned that waiting for wage pass-through to become visible could leave policy too late. The new tracker strengthens the case that the present energy shock has not yet generated a 2022-style wage-price cycle.

British household and business borrowing remained resilient before the Bank of England’s July 30 decision. Mortgage approvals recovered to 58,200 in June from a more than 2-year low in May, exceeding the 57,100 forecast but remaining below the 6-month average of 61,435. Net unsecured credit increased to £1.8 billion from £1.7 billion, including a £300 million rise in credit-card borrowing to £900 million, while lending to businesses increased to £1.5 billion from £1.1 billion.

Those flows coexist with substantially higher financing costs. The average 5-year fixed mortgage rate reached 5.66% on July 29, compared with 4.83% before the U.S. and Israel attacked Iran in February. The BOE is expected to hold as it balances weak aggregate growth against renewed energy inflation, but the borrowing figures offer little evidence that higher rates have already caused an abrupt contraction in household or business credit.

Canada’s central-bank deliberations revealed a more even division. Officials held the policy rate at 2.25% for a sixth meeting earlier in July and judged that the trade-off between weak growth and inflation had diminished as the economy adjusted to recent shocks. The bank expects growth to accelerate from 0.7% in 2026 to 1.8% in both 2027 and 2028, but council members disagreed over whether the recovery would broaden and endure.

Some Bank of Canada officials also noted an upward drift in medium-term inflation expectations. Excess capacity, slow unit-labor-cost growth and weaker rent inflation were restraining services prices, offsetting some of the effect of higher gasoline costs. The meeting preceded both renewed U.S.-Iran escalation and Trump’s threat of additional tariffs on Canadian goods, leaving the bank’s comfortable hold vulnerable to shocks on both sides of its mandate.

Brazil delivered firmer labor data before an expected Aug. 5 rate cut. The economy created 145,161 formal jobs in June, above the 115,000 median estimate, led by services and agriculture. Inflation nevertheless slowed to 4.52% in early July from 4.8% in mid-June, with prices rising only 0.06% during the month. Economists still expect a fourth consecutive 25-basis-point reduction to 14%, but stronger employment and pre-election fiscal support argue against a long easing sequence.

## Forward Market Significance

The next U.S. inflation and labor-cost releases will determine whether the July hold represented a temporary pause or a more durable reliance on market tightening. The Q2 Employment Cost Index on July 31 is the clearest scheduled test of domestic wage pressure. A firm result would reinforce the three dissenters’ argument that policy should tighten even if the energy shock remains volatile; a softer reading would support the governors who preferred to observe how higher market yields affect activity.

The Treasury curve now offers separate tests at each end. The 2-year yield reflects reduced urgency for September, while the rise in 10- and 30-year yields reflects greater compensation for inflation and duration. If incoming data strengthen the immediate hike case, the front end can reverse without requiring another increase in long inflation compensation. If the data soften while oil remains high, the curve may stay steep because a later Fed response would not remove the longer-run price risk.

The U.S.-Iran conflict remains capable of changing that distribution before the data settle it. Restored diplomacy and more reliable passage through Hormuz would reduce the pressure on breakevens. Further attacks on military sites, tankers or alternative export routes would confront the Fed with crude already more than 20% higher over a month and a Treasury market whose long end no longer responds automatically to falling equities.

The quarterly refunding will bring the supply question into the same debate. Unchanged auction-size guidance would avoid immediately validating expectations of greater duration issuance. Any adjustment that brings larger coupon sales closer would test whether the 30-year yield above 5.2% is sufficient compensation when fiscal borrowing and corporate issuance are competing for the same long-duration capital.

AI credit faces more immediate transaction deadlines. Orders for CoreWeave’s $2.6 billion loan are due Thursday after the borrower raised the spread to as much as 550 basis points, increased the discount to 97 and strengthened documentation. Demand at those terms will show whether investors consider take-or-pay contracts adequate protection against a leveraged expansion cycle or require still more compensation.

The possible $5.4 billion QTS financing provides the next high-grade data-center test. Its execution will be judged against the fall in QTS’s recent loan and the widening of its April bond from roughly 138 to 239 basis points over Treasuries. A delayed sale would preserve flexibility for the issuer; a completed deal would establish how much new-issue premium is required after July’s record high-grade supply.

The Bank of England decides on July 30. Its hold is widely expected, leaving the inflation assessment and treatment of higher energy costs more important than the policy rate itself. Mortgage rates at 5.66% have not prevented a recovery in approvals or continued consumer and business borrowing, so officials have limited evidence that existing restraint has produced a decisive weakening in demand.

The Bank of Japan follows on July 31. A hold after June’s increase to 1% remains the expected outcome, but the recommended 4.9% minimum-wage increase strengthens the evidence that pay gains are spreading. Guidance will need to reconcile that wage momentum with the effect of high import costs and the volatility that has pushed a major domestic pension investor toward active JGB management.

Australia’s next RBA meeting on Aug. 11 will test whether the softer trimmed-mean CPI was sufficient to end the year’s tightening cycle. The downside surprise and 11-basis-point fall in the 3-year yield favor patience, but 4.9% non-tradable inflation and renewed oil pressure leave another increase plausible rather than eliminated.

For credit investors, the broader test is whether the repricing remains concentrated in AI-related borrowers or further degrades investment-grade market functioning. The New York Fed’s high-grade distress measure, wider technology CDS, richer loan terms and stronger lender protections all point to diminished borrower power. Continued access for SBI and SoftBank shows that capital has not disappeared, but the price, maturity and documentation of each transaction are becoming more discriminating.

The July 29 close left the market with less uncertainty about the decision already made and more uncertainty about how restraint will be delivered. The Fed declined to raise the overnight rate, the front end rallied and the dollar fell. Oil, breakevens and the long end moved the other way. Until inflation data, energy supply or policy guidance provide a firmer anchor, the market itself is setting a higher price for long-term borrowing.

section_summaries.market_read: The close separated reduced urgency for the next Fed increase from a higher market price for long-term inflation and duration risk.
section_summaries.summary: The Fed hold relieved the front end but left the market to impose restraint farther out the curve. With the 10-year real yield nearly unchanged, rising breakevens accounted for almost all of the nominal 10-year selloff as renewed conflict lifted oil and investors questioned whether verbal resolve and three dissents were enough to contain longer-run inflation.

section_summaries.market_read: Treating higher bond yields as a substitute for policy action can sustain the very term premium that gives the Fed room to wait.
section_summaries.section_title: The Fed Relieves the Front End and Loses the Long End
section_summaries.summary: The Fed’s 9-3 hold removed the risk of an immediate increase but exposed a broader tightening bloc and provided little guidance for September. Warsh argued that higher market borrowing costs were already doing some of the Fed’s work, leaving long-duration investors to determine the necessary restraint without a firm policy anchor.

section_summaries.market_read: Weaker equities and higher long yields jointly tightened financial conditions through lower wealth and more expensive long-term borrowing.
section_summaries.section_title: Renewed Fighting Restores the Energy Inflation Premium
section_summaries.summary: Renewed U.S.-Iran fighting abruptly ended a three-session oil respite, with Brent and WTI surging as attacks, vulnerable shipping routes and depleted inventories restored the risk of another supply disruption. Higher breakevens, a weaker dollar and falling long Treasuries showed that investors treated the escalation primarily as an inflation shock rather than a conventional flight to safety.

section_summaries.market_read: Repeated data-center financings are competing for long-duration capital as investors reassess leverage, customer concentration and asset returns.
section_summaries.section_title: AI Borrowing Strain Moves Beyond Individual Deals
section_summaries.summary: AI financing strain spread across official market-functioning measures, credit protection, loans and prospective bond supply. Record July investment-grade issuance coincided with weaker technology credit, while CoreWeave offered richer pricing and stronger documentation and recent QTS debt traded below issue levels. Other borrowers still raised capital, but buyers increasingly dictated price, maturity and creditor protections.

section_summaries.section_title: Global Inflation Data Complicate the Tightening Cycle
section_summaries.summary: Australia’s softer core inflation reduced expectations of another 2026 increase, while Japan’s proposed 4.9% minimum-wage rise supported eventual normalization. Slower euro-area wage growth eased pressure on the ECB, but resilient British borrowing, divided Canadian officials and firm Brazilian employment showed that energy inflation is reaching economies with very different demand conditions.

section_summaries.market_read: Softer data may not flatten the curve if oil stays high, while firmer data could reverse the front-end rally without lifting long breakevens again.
section_summaries.summary: The July hold shifted the question from whether the Fed would tighten immediately to how restraint will be delivered. U.S. wage data, the path of the U.S.-Iran conflict and demand for AI financing will test whether front-end relief can persist while oil, inflation compensation and long-term borrowing costs remain elevated.

overall_summary.headline: Fed hold rallies the front end as inflation risk drives a long-end selloff
overall_summary.session_narrative:
Treasuries split sharply after the Fed held rates for a fifth meeting. The 2-year yield fell 1.4 basis points to 4.274% as Chair Kevin Warsh declined to signal a September increase and said higher market yields were already restraining the economy. The 10-year yield rose 7.2 basis points to 4.679%, while the 30-year jumped 11.3 basis points to 5.203%, steepening the 2s30s curve by 12.7 basis points.

The long-end selloff was driven primarily by inflation compensation: the 10-year breakeven rose 7.5 basis points to 2.27%, while the real yield was nearly unchanged. Three Fed officials dissented in favor of a quarter-point increase, and renewed U.S.-Iran fighting sent Brent up 7.37% and WTI up 6.35%, reversing the oil relief that had supported Treasuries during the previous three sessions.

Weak equities did not produce a conventional haven rally. Technology shares led the decline and volatility rose, yet long Treasuries also fell as investors demanded more compensation for inflation and duration. Record July investment-grade issuance and increasingly costly AI financing added pressure to long-duration credit.
overall_summary.summary: The Fed left rates at 3.5% to 3.75% and reduced the urgency of a September increase, but three hawkish dissents, reliance on market-led restraint and renewed U.S.-Iran fighting pushed inflation compensation and long Treasury yields sharply higher.
